name: Clean Code
description: Enforces clean code principles including single responsibility, meaningful naming, and DRY.
content:
# Clean Code Rules

- Follow the Single Responsibility Principle — each function and class should do one thing well
- Use meaningful, descriptive names — variable names should reveal intent without comments
- Keep functions small — under 20 lines is a good target, extract when longer
- DRY (Don't Repeat Yourself) but don't abstract prematurely — wait for 3 repetitions before extracting
- Avoid deep nesting — use early returns and guard clauses to reduce indentation
- Write code that reads like prose — prefer clarity over cleverness
- Delete dead code — don't comment it out, that's what version control is for
- Keep function arguments to 3 or fewer — use an options object for more
- Separate commands from queries — functions should either do something or return something, not both
- Write comments only for "why", never for "what" — the code itself should explain what it does
